text: I’m a mixed-race black/white/Latino guy, living in the Seattle area which is a temperate rainforest technically. I have combo dry skin and I was traveling in SE Asia, Germany, Spain, the American SW, so places where I needed sunscreen and was wearing shorts and T-shirts most of the time. Reviews are all copied and pasted below but also in the slides. Biore Uv Aqua Rich Watery Essence 🇯🇵 - 9/10 Absorbs well. Has a bit of a grainy quality but it’s extremely slight. Doesn’t really add moisture to the skin. Fine to reapply during the day and waterproof. Never used on face. Biore Athlizm Spray 🇯🇵 - 6/10 It’s fine, it is just a bad value for the money. The spray evaporates really quickly so it’s hard to tell where you applied it. Must prefer the cream Biore Athlizm Cream 🇯🇵 - 9/10 Really the GOAT for anything outdoor, sweaty or swimming. You feel like a duck with it on. It stuck all day when I was in Singapore or swimming in the hottest days in Seattle. Not an everyday sunscreen, but the best for what it does. Haruharu wonder black rice airyfit 🇰🇷 - 3/10 It piles on the face and body for me. Not waterproof so maybe best in winter. It may have to do with me putting too much on, but despite all the hype around it, wouldn’t buy it again Nivea UV super water gel 🇯🇵 - 8/10 goes on very easily and disappears into the skin. Like the pump that you can refill. Not waterproof so prob best for winter/cooler months. Mediheal Madecassoside moisture sun serum 🇰🇷 - 7/10 Applies as a liquid but absorbs instantly. You don’t need to reapply during the day. Waterproof and pretty much invisible. It does pill like every other Korean sunscreen on me. Wish it didn’t. Holika Holika aloe waterproof sunscreen 🇰🇷 - 9/10 Smells pleasant like aloe vera. Ok to reapply throughout the day without piling. Leaves a very slight white cast in the elbow but that’s about all I can say bad about it. Didn’t use it on my face. House of Hur Weightless 🇰🇷 - 5/10 No smell. Goes on very liquid and disappears with no glow. It seems to pill on the face around the neck but not on the body. Senka UV water Gel 🇯🇵 - 7/10 It goes on a bit sticky but does dry. Leaves a white cast as it has zinc oxide in it. Def feels waterproof. Would use this in hot weather or swimming for sure. No smell. Fine to reapply. Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Aqua Fresh 🇰🇷 - 5/10 It pills on the face, back of the neck and ears but it’s fine on the body. Feels like lotion on the body so I like that. KISS ME MOMMY! UV Aqua Milk Sunscreen SPF50+ PA++++ 🇯🇵 - 8/10 It’s waterproof, it dissolves into the skin, it’s great for the face. It does pill a little bit on my neck when I reapplied. It has no scent and it’s mild enough to use on a 1 year old baby. SCINIC Enjoy Super Mild Sun Essence 🇰🇷 - 8/10 Great on first application, but it does pile on second application after a while. No white cast. No smell. Very light. Not waterproof. Does pile less than some others, will try applying less. Really want to love this one! Nivea UV Super Water Essence EX 🇯🇵 - 9/10 Wonderful smell. Goes on like a creamy gel then disappears. Fine to reapply. Love it! Fine on face, but it is pretty shiny. Skin Aqua Super Moisture UV Gel 🇯🇵 - 10/10 Great on face or body. Fine to reapply without pilling as it is a fine gel-like cream. Not too shiny. Waterproof. Very moisturizing ingredient list so works as a lotion. Might be perfect. Biore Aqua Rich Watery Gel 🇯🇵 1/10 - Has titanium dioxide which immediately made me look sickly white. It also pills up on the skin after first application with no other product underneath. I thought I couldn’t dislike any Japanese sunscreen but here I am. Nivea Deep Protect & Care gel 🇯🇵 - 8/10 Feels very moisturizing on my skin. I like the scent but it does smell like mosquito repellent when you put it on. Don’t know if I’m going to try it on face for that reason. Feels like I have nothing on after applying. Really good body sunscreen. Biore UV Aqua Rich Airy Hold Cream 🇯🇵 - 5/10 Goes on very thick, like soft serve ice cream or Greek yogurt. At first it leaves a white tint, but you can rub it in. It doesn’t feel moisturizing per se but def feels like it’s sticking to your skin. Has titanium dioxide so I don’t think I’d use it on my face. I’ll use it up on my body but wouldn’t buy again. Nivea UV Super Water Gel Ex 🇯🇵 - 10/10 Big ass bottle at 270g. Good deals on Yami. Goes on matte. Fine to reapply. Need to try on face. Tage Cica-Tree Water Jelly Sun Serum 🇰🇷 - 6/10 It’s ok. It does pill a little around the folds of my neck upon reapplication, but that’s it. It goes on a bit shiny. The consistency is a bit chunky so it doesn’t come out of the tube consistently. It can come out a lot at once and it’s impossible to avoid. Wouldn’t buy again. Nivea Men Uv Protector 🇯🇵 - 4/10 Too small. Smells funny. Pills on me on first application. Kose Suncut Uv Perfect Essence 🇯🇵 - 7/10 Great size. Really moisturizing. Goes into skin and beard well. It does pill a little around my neck after reapplication. Great ingredients like Squalane and other soothing extracts. Hatomugi UV care and moisturizing spf 50+ 🇯🇵 - 9/10 Big bottle. Very pleasant feeling and smell on the skin. Seemed fine on face. Doesn’t seem to be waterproof but great for daily use. Nivea UV Super Water Essence Ex 🇯🇵 - 10/10 Really just as good as the gel. Slightly more moisturizing and a little less product for the money. Regardless, you put it on and a second later you’d never know it was on your face. Can reapply all day without pilling

text: Hello all! I am back again for another review roundup of my empties. My skin type is quite dry; I used to be (knock on wood) very acne prone but I’ve been on spironolactone for the last ~6 months and it seems to really have knocked it out. My primary skin concerns are indented acne scarring and PIE. I am pale as a ghost. ***THE GOOD, BUT COULD BE IMPROVED:*** - **Dr. Althea 147 Barrier Cream (2026 reformulation)**: I posted a review of this product before - I went through two tubes of the old formulation and really really liked it. When I received this latest tube I found that it had been reformulated, I think to remove some botanical extracts, etc. that people possibly found irritating. I couldn’t find the ingredient list of the old product, but I would also venture to guess that the silicone content has been brought way down in the new formulation. It’s not a horrible change and I understand why they did it, but I think the new version is way less special/unique. I loved the silicone-y, primer-like finish of the old one - perfect for AM use - while still being restorative and nourishing. I used the old one AM and PM while I was using tazarotene and I was totally fine. The new one feels like it sinks in better and has a very skin-like finish but doesn’t feel as overall nourishing to me. Overall, this is still one of my favorite lightweight moisturizers but I consider the reformulation to be a downgrade. - **Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream**: I get why this is so popular… but it just wasn’t for me. Obviously, it’s huge and cheap which is amazing - I used this freely on my face/neck/chest and a bit on my body. I also really liked/preferred the more matte finish of this moisturizer as compared to my current HG, the GOAT, Aestura 365 Barrier Cream. But - the Illiyoon just has a chemically/plasticky smell that is very unpleasant. It also didn’t feel as moisturizing/nourishing/soothing as my girl Aestura. I stopped being able to use tazarotene while I was using this, though *for now* I am attributing it to my skin changing from the spironolactone - but I am getting ready to try restarting a retinoid with a different moisturizer, so we’ll see. Overall, I wasn’t mad about this moisturizer, but I’m glad to move on. - **Hatomugi SPF 31 PA+++ UV milky gel**: I almost put this in a GOAT category because I do think it’s freaking great for what it is. It’s cheap, big, and in a pump bottle for easy application. It has a lovely light but not overpowering scent, and it’s thin and lightweight; just a dream to apply. The only drawback (and it’s kinda a big one) is that it’s only SPF 31 and PA+++, so I wouldn’t use this on my face/neck/chest bc I need to protect ‘em better than that. But this is sooo nice and easy to just slop onto my arms in the morning (and I’m not usually the most consistent with sunscreen on my arms). I will probably repurchase for that purpose unless someone recommends an alternative higher-protection option. - **Wardah Lip Barrier SPF 30**: this is an Indonesian brand; picked up this product when I was there for vacation recently. When I first bought this, I thought I had found heaven; I was calculating how many I should smuggle into my bag back home. It’s just super lightweight, not glossy/sticky, with NO sunscreen taste whatsoever. However… it ended up really drying my lips out pretty quickly; I have to alternate it with other more moisturizing lip SPF options (current favorite is the Prequel Lip Visor - but it’s so glossy). This saddened me but also I can’t buy this brand in the US so I guess it’s for the best. - **Nivea Deep Moisture Melty Type**: OK this is very nice…but imperfect. It is definitely moisturizing and feels good on the lips, but doesn’t last a crazy long time. It smells nice but has a VERY distinct sunscreen taste (this is my main problem with it). Idk. Let me know if you have other lip SPF recs because I feel like it could get better than this! ***THE TRASH HEAP:*** - **Shiseido Ultimate Sun Protector Lotion Mineral SPF 60+**: This is a US formulation so I understand Shiseido is working with limitations here. That said, this has to be one of the worst sunscreens on god’s green earth. The formulators and packaging designers of this product should answer for their crimes. This is a liquid formulation but feels absolutely disgusting to apply and wear. Greasy, never rubs in or dries down, with a greyish white cast the likes of which I’m not sure I’ve ever experienced (as mentioned earlier, I am Casper-esque; I’ve tried a LOT of mineral sunscreens and I’m usually fine). However, THE PACKAGING is the greatest crime here in my opinion. SHISEDO - I KNOW YOU OWN ANESSA SO I KNOW YOU CAN DO BETTER. It has a flimsy flip-top that has just an open hole that the liquid sunscreen leaks out of - no nozzle for a targeted application. This is LITERALLY impossible to apply without getting it everywhere, and you will unavoidably have white crusty stains around the edges of your clothes as this migrates and slops around. I took this big, cumbersome, shitty bottle on my recent beach vacation just to use it up on my body (the one and only redeeming factor is that it is water-resistant). I used the entire thing and hated every minute of it.
label: review

text: I am mostly into skincare brands and I've noticed two tricks Korean brands use which make me angry. Both of them are related to INCI and product content. # Claim ingredients are added in tiny portion just to justify mention on the label. Thanks to [South Korea's Cosmetics Act Enforcement Rule](https://www.law.go.kr/lsLinkProc.do?chrClsCd=010202&datClsCd=010102&gubun=admRul&joNo=001900003&lsId=37973&lsNm=%ED%99%94%EC%9E%A5%ED%92%88%EB%B2%95%EC%8B%9C%ED%96%89%EA%B7%9C%EC%B9%99&mode=10) (link leads to list of rules in Korean, can be translated on-site with browser) the brands should disclose concentration of marketing ingredients used in names. And now we see this trick precisely on the label. Let's take [Farm Stay Collagen Water Full Moist Cream Toner](https://inkeedecoder.com/products/farmstay-collagen-water-full-moist-cream-toner) as an example (link leads to full INCI). They claim it is a collagen toner, but if we check INCI: **Hydrolyzed Collagen (55Ppm).** PPM means "Parts per million" and it is another trick to think the content is higher that it is. 1PPM == 0.0001%, which means collagen content in mentioned toner is 0.0055%. Drop in a barrel just to be able to use ingredient name in the name and trick buyers. Other companies may use PPB (parts per billion) or mg (milligrams) to have higher number and make you believe there is enough of ingredient inside. Sure, 1000ppb looks better than 0.0001%. I don't think only Korean companies do this, but Korean companies are obligated to disclose the content of marketed ingredient, so now we can see this. Mostly sure EU brands do this too, but we can only speculate since there is no such rule in place (too bad!). # Spoiler ingredients (my own term). Brands utilize 1% INCI rule to make you believe the product is reach in great ingredients. Many people know the golden INCI rule: ingredients are listed in decreased order of content by mass relative to each other. Meaning if we take all ingredients, weight them and sort in decreasing order - this will be the list. That's why Water usually comes first - it simply takes the most space in most of the products. But not many known that INCI rule allow to list ingredients below 1% in ANY order. This is called 1% rule. And manufacturers utilize this to trick us. What manufacturers do: - Add many claim or popular ingredients as <0.01% content - Move them closer to ingredients >1% in the list - Move "nasty" non-popular ingredients (like preservatives) to the end of the list Next two INCI lists correspond to the same product and both are totally valid to put on the label: > **INCI 1:** Water, Glycerin (5%), Propylene Glycol (3%), Phenoxyethanol (0.9%), Xanthan Gum (0.7%), Allantoin (0.5%), Retinol (0.1%). > **INCI2:** Water, Glycerin (5%), Propylene Glycol (3%), Retinol (0.1%), Allantoin (0.5%), Xanthan Gum (0.7%), Phenoxyethanol (0.9%). Have you spotted how I moved the preservative to the end of the list and placed Retinol closer to the start? Now if you don't know the percentages you gonna assume that if Retinol is closer to the beginning of the list then there is more of it than Allantoin. That's why the only way to know active ingredient content is product labeling. Manufacturer should literally say "Retinol 0.1% serum". I see this technique is abused a lot by several Korean brands. They add many extracts in 0.01% content and move them closer to 1% line. This makes the whole list longer and makes you think that the product is rich and first few ingredients are in very high content. Sorry for the long post, but I haven't found better way to explain this. What tricks do you notice and hate the most?
label: discussion

text: Hi everyone! I’ve been using the Allie Sheer Ecru sunscreen for maybe two months now, hoping it would help with my rosacea-prone skin, which can get quite red. **The Pros:** **General feel:** It's generally a quite nice sunscreen. The texture is decent and it doesn't feel overly oily on the skin. **Toning:** It does a great job of evening out my skin tone and toning down the redness from my rosacea, which was my main goal. For this reason, I can see it being good for someone with similar concerns. **The Cons:** **Finish:** While it's not super oily, I wouldn't call the finish matte. It definitely has a more natural, slightly dewy look. So if you're looking for a strictly matte finish, this might not be it. **The major drawback:** The reason I'm writing this review is the pooling in creases, and I've attached photos to show exactly what I mean. I found that this sunscreen pools significantly in the creases of my eyes. This creates very pronounced light lines where it has settled. When I care enough about what I look like, I’ll add some no Sibum powder before applying my light foundation, and that usually prevents this from happening to this extreme, but it doesn’t prevent it entirely. **Overall Verdict:** I want to love this sunscreen for its toning properties, but the pronounced pooling is a major dealbreaker for me. Right now, I'm just using this on days when I work from home and no one can see it on Zoom. I probably wouldn't recommend it for anyone whose eyelids crease unless you’re prepared to put in a lot of effort to make it stick in place.
